{"self_assessment": "Impact: The fish reads as a fish on the table: a long body from the start out to the tail, a top fin off the back, and a lower arm closing the tail. The top fin is the feature I owned, and it should help the judge place the animal. I can't say for certain the outline will be recognised, though. The tail was re-laid late and the final joins were checked in a hurry, not confirmed before the push.

Execution: I laid the top fin (stroke 4) only once the top edge had grown past its branch point, and my inspection confirmed it traces back to the start. The lower arm I laid from Maya's nudged join and called it standing. My weak spot was timing: I called the top fin down while Tom was still laying the tail, so my call-outs got ahead of what was actually on the table. I should have checked before announcing. Holding back from placing more near the push was the right call.

Collaboration: I kept my hands off stroke 2 while Tom redid the tail, and I answered when he asked me to take the lower arm. When my first inspection got lost under Maya's talk, I sent it again so the others could check the joins. I could have offered to take the last dominoes at the tip sooner, since I was free and watching.

Leadership: I didn't lead much here. I followed Priya's plan and didn't push changes. Where I did step in, I reported what I saw rather than directing anyone. Next time I'd flag a gap in the plan, like the tail being laid from the wrong end, sooner, instead of letting others catch it."}
